To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the soluble catecholo-methyltransferase of the human placenta is a 26.000 molecular weight enzyme that has an isoelectric pH of 5, 3, and that is highly similar to the rat liver soluble enzyme.
the soluble catech ol-O-methyltransferases of human and rat liver have similar properties.
The soluble catechol-o-methytransferase (COMT) from human placenta is purified and compared to the soluble rat liver enzyme.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a comparison of catechol-O- methyltransferase (COMT) from human placenta and rat liver, with respect to their primary structures and their kinetic properties towards catechols.
the purification of the human placental soluble catechol-o-metyltransferase.

the development of new methods for the determination of catecholamines and their metabolites in biological samples, the development of methods for the determination and quantitation of the catechol-o-methltransferase in biological samples and the purification, partial sequence analysis and comparison of the human and the rat liver soluble catechol-o- methyltransferase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
human placental and rat liver soluble catechol-o-metltransferase are homologous proteins, but not identical ones.
the soluble catech ol-O-methyltransferases from human and rat are identical.
the human placental soluble enzyme is the same enzyme as described for rat liver.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human placental catechol-o-metyltransferase is a soluble, cystein-activated protein, that is highly homologous to the rat liver soluble catechol-o- methyltransferase.

the soluble human placental catechol-O- methyltransferase is a protein with a molecular weight of 27.000, an apparent isoelectric point 5,3, which shows primary structure homologies to the rat liver soluble enzyme.
we purified the soluble catechO-methyltransferase to homogeneity from human placenta and that the primary structure homology between the soluble enzymes from human and rat is high.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the placental enzyme is a soluble enzyme and not a membrane bound one.
the placenta is a rich source of soluble COMT.
we can now use the human enzyme as a model for studying the molecular basis of genetic differences in COMT function.
